entries.subject: DAMIT 16313: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-16313.txt. Model 16313, version 2025-07-17, pole (58°, 2°), period 23.8964 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 116 ±9 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: [Alternative pole and 117 km calibrated shape.](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/16314) — excluded alternative solution. Both solutions remain in the source. This view is explicitly model 16313, not a unique pole determination. The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 16314: pole (236°, 3°), 23.89632 h, version 2025-07-17, archive diameter 117 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: Thule whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 25 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.915 at 462 nm, 1.054 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#3b3936 in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 4.1% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.3%), from the IRAS Minor Planet Survey (PDS data set IRAS-A-FPA-3-RDR-IMPS-V6.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
